# RiskDesk — Risks Not In VaR (quantified limitations)

*Generated by `python -m risk.jobs.rniv` from the committed snapshot; as of 2026-08-06, 17 factors, firm 1-day VaR99 $1,168,047 / ES97.5 $1,181,538. Every number below regenerates from the repository alone. Materiality: Material >= 5% of the base measure, Monitor >= 1%, else Immaterial. (The database path stores levels and quantities at fixed decimal precision; its firm VaR is $1,168,055.33 - the ~7e-6 relative gap to the float path here is quantization, measured and understood.)*

Banks keep an inventory of risks their VaR model does not capture, each
with a measured impact and a treatment. This is that inventory for
RiskDesk: every entry quantifies a limitation from `docs/model_doc.md`
section 5 against the same snapshot the model runs on.

| ID | §5 | Risk | Measured impact | Class | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | 1 | sqrt(10) horizon scaling vs overlapping 10-day revaluation | -$726,038 on the 10-day VaR (-19.7%) | Material | Report scaled figure with this measured gap; overlapping estimator kept as a check |
| R2 | 4 | Asynchronous closes understate cross-asset co-movement | diversification benefit 40.3% at 1 day vs 39.3% at 2 days (+1.0%p of hidden co-movement) | Immaterial | Named bias; synchronization overlay out of scope for public daily data |
| R3 | 5 | Forward-fill zero returns damp EWMA vol | $24,257 on FHS VaR (+1.9%) | Monitor | Fill share and per-factor ratios recorded; bounded by DQ fill caps |
| R4 | 8 | Fixed stressed window vs candidate crisis windows | in-force $2,737,390 is the max of the candidates (COVID year $1,911,190, 2022 hiking year $2,104,569) | Immaterial | Programmatic worst-window search is the roadmap replacement |
| R5 | 11 | Position concentration of firm ES | top position 33.9% of firm ES, top 3 79.5% | Monitor | Euler components monitored; factor-model idiosyncratic add-on on the roadmap |
| R6 | 9 | 1bp post-shock yield floor | unbinding; minimum post-shock yield 2.31% (230bp of headroom) | Immaterial | Re-measure if front-end yields fall below ~1.5% |

## R1 — Horizon scaling

The reported 10-day VaR is the 1-day figure times sqrt(10) ($3,693,689). Revaluing the book on 491 overlapping 10-day shock vectors from the same 500-day window gives $2,967,651 (-19.7%), and ES $2,904,578 vs $3,736,351 scaled. Overlap leaves ~50 effectively independent draws, so this is an estimate with real sampling noise - the point is the sign and rough size of the iid error, not a replacement model.

## R2 — Asynchronous closes

Two-day aggregation restores co-movement that different close times split across days: the diversification benefit drops from 40.3% at 1 day to 39.3% at 2 days - that gap is co-movement the daily correlation structure cannot see, and it is the cleaner isolation of the sync effect. (The raw 2-day overlapping VaR, $1,570,859 vs $1,651,868 sqrt(2)-scaled (-4.9%), carries the same drift and overlap effects as R1 and is reported for completeness only.) Largest equity-to-next-day spillovers (corr at lag +1 vs same-day):

- EQ.SPY -> FX.GBPUSD: lag+1 +0.23 vs same-day +0.14
- EQ.SPY -> FX.MXNUSD: lag+1 +0.18 vs same-day +0.20
- EQ.MSFT -> FX.EURUSD: lag+1 +0.16 vs same-day +0.07

## R3 — Forward-fill vol damping

Filled cells are 3.64% of factor-days in the 500-day window. Recomputing each factor's EWMA forecast on print-days only and rescaling the FHS scenario set moves firm FHS VaR from $1,299,508 to $1,323,765 (+1.9%). Largest per-factor forecast ratios:

- FX.MXNUSD: 1.153
- FX.EURUSD: 1.148
- FX.GBPUSD: 1.148

## R4 — Stressed-window choice

Stressed ES on today's book under each candidate calibration window:

- GFC year (in force): $2,737,390
- COVID year: $1,911,190
- 2022 hiking year: $2,104,569

The in-force window remains the worst of the candidates - currently conservative (+0.0% vs the worst candidate). The programmatic search over full 2007+ history replaces this check.

## R6 — Yield floor

Across the full 500-day scenario set and the GFC replay, the minimum post-shock yield is 2.31% - 230bp above the 0.01% pricing floor. The floor currently truncates nothing.
